_comment: Phase 3 depth and light. Level id -> which backdrop world it uses, how much air is in front of that backdrop, how far each tile layer is knocked back, and where the lights are. levels/*.json is geometry only and did not change for this phase; this is the mood, kept apart from it so an artist can re-light the game without touching a single tile.

_fields.air: haze quad drawn over the parallax and behind the tiles: ramp step + alpha
_fields.bg_tint: multiplier on the background tile layer: ramp step for the hue, mix for how much of that hue, scale for how far back it sits
_fields.fg_tint: the same for the solid layer. Keep it near 1.0 - this is what the player reads as ground
_fields.vignette: 0..1 strength of the screen-edge darkening, drawn over the tiles and under the entities
_fields.lights: additive pools at tile coordinates. radius in px, intensity 0..1, flicker 0..1
_fields.emissive: tile id -> a pool on every one of those tiles, merged along a row

_colours: Every ramp/step pair indexes assets/palette.json, which tools/art/palette.py generates. No RGB literals: an ambient tint multiplies the whole screen, so it has to come off the same ramps as the art.

jungle_1._note: CANOPY TRAIL. Daylight. The backdrop does the work; the air is only thick enough to keep the far trees behind the tiles.

jungle_2._note: ROOT HOLLOW. The dark one. Its bg layer is a solid wall of bg_rock on every screen, so the parallax is never visible here - all of the depth is tint, vignette and the lights that pick out the route.

jungle_3._note: THE WATERWAY. Also walled in bg_rock, so again no parallax. The water surface lights itself: every run of water_top gets one pool.

jungle_4._note: SKY BRANCH. The bright one. The haze is pale rather than dark, which is the whole trick: it lifts the backdrop towards the sky instead of pushing it towards black.

jungle_5._note: HEART OF THE GROVE. The boss arena: same jungle backdrop as CANOPY TRAIL, pushed violet so the last level does not look like the first one.

ruins_1._note: DROWNED STEPS. The first of the sunken world, so it is the one that has to *introduce* it: the ruins backdrop - a drowned colonnade going blue with distance - is left as readable as it ever gets here, and the haze is only thick enough to sit the stone behind the tiles.

ruins_2._note: THE COLONNADE. The level is a colonnade and so is the backdrop, so this is the one screen in the game where the parallax and the tiles are the same architecture receding. The tint keeps them apart by value rather than by hue.

ruins_3._note: TIDE GALLERY. Half the level is under water and the currents run through it, so the surface does the lighting: every run of water_top gets its own pool, exactly as THE WATERWAY does.

ruins_4._note: THE CISTERN. Enclosed and flooded - the darkest of the five. The haze is nearly black water and the vignette closes the walls in; the only thing that gives light back is the surface itself.

ruins_5._note: THE TIDE MAW. The arena floods and drains under the player, so the light has to move with it: the pools are on the water surface, not on the walls, and they rise and fall with the tide because the tile they are attached to does.

heights_1._note: UPDRAFT. First screen of world 3 and the one that has to sell the altitude, so it gets the least air of the five: the heights backdrop - a dusk sky over snow peaks standing out of a sea of cloud - is meant to be looked at here.

heights_2._note: THE THERMALS. The vents are what lift you, so they are the only thing in the level that emits: a low ember pool on every heights_vent, merged along a row, which reads as heat coming off the rock rather than as a lamp.

heights_3._note: ASH COLUMN. The dim one: ash in the air rather than haze, so the backdrop is pushed towards the ember ramp instead of towards black and the peaks go the colour of the sky.

heights_4._note: THE LONG GLIDE. The brightest screen in the game. Eleven hundred cloud tiles, almost no vignette and the palest haze there is: nothing here should read as a ceiling.

heights_5._note: THE STORMCREST. Same peaks as the other four, under weather. The air goes stone grey and the vignette closes in, which is what makes the bird - drawn on the stone ramp itself - read by silhouette instead of by colour.

deeps_1._note: THE LIGHTLESS. World 4's teacher. `darkness` is one alpha for the whole level, so 'starts lit and descends into the dark' is built out of authored pools rather than out of the shade: six in the mouth, graded eastward (0.58 at the sinkhole's foot, 0.38, then 0.22 at the threshold) so the daylight is visibly behind her before anything is asked. Screens B and D carry no authored light at all -- everything that glows down there is a tile, which is why it can be captured and argued about. deep_fungus (269) marks the route, luminous_wall (214) marks the secret she cannot open yet, and deep_spore (267) marks the only two things that can hurt her: a dark hazard you cannot see is not a lesson, it is a coin toss. The exit gets the one warm pool in screen C, because a lit doorway is what this level teaches her to look for. darkness 0.88 / vignette 0.40 and the 214 and 267 entries are World 4's measured house recipe, not this level's choices.

deeps_2._note: CHEW THROUGH. The second level of the world, so it is dim rather than black: darkness 0.70 against the world's 0.88 keeps a wall four tiles ahead legible, because this is the level that has to teach you that some walls are not walls. The only emitter is the luminous wall at the vault (214), an fg tile, merged along its run -- the one wall here with a room behind it is the one you can see from across the chamber.

deeps_3._note: THE GALLERIES. A ring of six chambers, and the light is what tells you which one you are in: the pools mark the chambers the ring runs through, graded down from the lit mouth to the dead rock, and everything off the ring is lit by tiles or not at all. deep_fungus (269) is the route marker, and 214 and 270 are the two chords that glow -- in a dark level the walls you can break are the walls you can see, and breaking one puts its light out. INTEGRATION NOTE: every scalar here is the author's; the seven pool POSITIONS were not committed anywhere and are placed on the chambers named in tools/worlds/deeps_3.py's docstring. See the M4 integration report.

deeps_4._note: SPORE LIGHT. The darkest level in the game, and the one where light is the resource: the haze is nearly black earth, the vignette closes the tunnel in, and every lamp is a tile. deep_fungus (269) is the violet mat the route is navigated by, pool to pool; luminous_wall (214) is the gold lamp that is also a wall, so breaking it puts it out; deep_glowwall (270) is the one breakable meant to be FOUND in the dark, so its violet fracture is a lamp in its own right - radius 24 reaches eight pixels past the neighbouring tile's centre and stops there. 0.74 is a measured readability floor and not a mood: at 0.86 an additive pool brightens rock and void by the same amount, so a solid tile and the air beside it are both 14% of themselves and the level cannot be read even inside the lantern.

deeps_5._note: THE BROOD QUEEN. The numbers are the world's, not invented here: darkness 0.88 and vignette 0.40 are the foundation agent's measured pair for a 74 px lantern, and the emissive recipe for tile 214 (gold 6, intensity 0.40, radius 30, lift 0) is the measured one for a luminous wall. This entry is not a suggestion -- tests/integration/boss_brood_queen_tests.gd holds it as a constant and `t_the_light_dies_with_the_wall` installs exactly this dictionary into the live level and measures what it does.

nest_1._note: BLACK GLASS. World 5's teacher, and the first level in the game whose subject is a lever. Cold glass lit from inside: the air is thin and dark so the backdrop stays behind the tiles, the fg tint is pushed one step towards ember rather than desaturated, and every pool is on something the player has to read -- the two levers, the trading wall's two doorways, the mouth of the flue, the slag gate's two ends and the exit. The emissive tiles are the level's own light and are all three of them SOLID, because AmbienceLayer._collect_emissive scans the fg: 281 obsidian_hot is the heat, banded around every nest_vein in the backdrop and run along the whole lower floor, so the deep half of the level is visibly the hot one; 287 nest_shard is the two pits, which glow for the reason deeps_1's spore does; 291 nest_crust is the single breakable, glowing once, which is how TERMITE DEEPS taught 'this wall is different'. 289 nest_vein is NOT in here: it is a background tile by its own art and emits nothing from back there, which is the point -- the flow is behind the glass and the glass is what you see.

nest_2._note: THE SWITCHYARD. World 5's second level and the first one whose subject is COMPOSITION: two levers, six doors, and most of the doors in rooms the lever cannot see. The light says which is which. GOLD pools sit on the two levers in the cabin and on all five gantry plugs plus the two yard doors -- the things a throw moves -- and EMBER pools sit on the three chutes and the two chain heads, which are the things that are always true. No `darkness` key: the dark is World 4's verb and this world's is the lever, so everything here is tint, vignette and the tiles that glow. The emissive entries are the level's own light and both are SOLID, because AmbienceLayer._collect_emissive scans the fg: 281 obsidian_hot is the heat banded around every nest_vein in the backdrop, and 287 nest_shard is the two pits, which glow for the reason deeps_1's spore does -- a hazard you cannot see is a coin toss. 289 nest_vein is NOT in here: it is a background tile by its own art and emits nothing from back there, which is the point.

nest_3._note: FOUR SHAPES. The working floor of the nest, and the one level in the world that is lit in four different rooms at once. EMBER is the room everywhere: the forge floor is the hottest thing in the level and the quench the coldest, which is the `bg_tint` doing the work rather than a second alpha. GOLD is reserved for what a throw moves or what you act on -- the two levers, and each of the four doors they move -- so the player can read the machine off the light. No `darkness` key: the dark is World 4's verb and this world's is the lever. The two emissive entries are the level's own light and both are SOLID, because AmbienceLayer._collect_emissive scans the fg: 281 obsidian_hot is the heat `_hot()` bands around every nest_vein, and 287 nest_shard is the trench, which glows for the reason deeps_1's spore does -- a hazard you cannot see is a coin toss. 289 nest_vein is NOT in here: it is a background tile by its own art and emits nothing from back there, which is the point.

nest_4._note: THE LAST ASCENT. The level is lit in two halves and the gap between them is the level's World 4 leg: cols 23-38 -- the flat, the comb and the fault -- carry NO authored pool at all, and everything that glows in there is a tile. That is not a mood, it is the only way this world can say 'dark stretch': `darkness` is one value for a whole level, World 5 does not use the key (nest_1's grammar), and a gradient does not exist. EMBER is the room, as everywhere in the nest. GOLD is reserved for what a throw moves or what you act on -- the two levers and the three doors they move -- so a player can read the machine off the light, and the two gold pools in the unlit half's neighbours (the flue's mouth at the landing, lever B in the hall) are the two things the dark stretch is navigated BETWEEN. The emissive pair is the level's own light and both are SOLID, because AmbienceLayer._collect_emissive scans the fg: 281 obsidian_hot is the heat `_hot()` bands around every nest_vein -- including the four in the fault, which is what marks its take-offs when nothing else does -- and 287 nest_shard is the shard bed, which glows for the reason deeps_1's spore does. 289 nest_vein is NOT in here: it is a background tile by its own art and emits nothing from back there, which is the point.

nest_5._note: THE OBSIDIAN HEART. The last room in the game, and the one the world's grammar was written for: world "obsidian", an ember room, gold reserved for the things you act on, and NO `darkness` key at all -- the nest is lit by what is burning in it. 281 obsidian_hot and 287 nest_shard are the emissive foreground tiles; 289 nest_vein is background dressing and stays unlit, because a vein that glowed would compete with the Heart. This entry is not a suggestion -- tests/integration/boss_obsidian_heart_tests.gd holds it as a constant and `t_the_hearthold_reads_as_an_ember_room` installs exactly this dictionary into the live level and measures what it does.

test_arena._note: Left neutral on purpose. tools/itest.sh plays here, and a test that has to be re-baselined every time someone re-lights a level is a test nobody trusts.
